_comment: Shared SPEC-023 §3.3.1 rule 9 rate-global rounding vectors. ONE source of truth consumed by scripts/tests/test_catalog_artifact_feed.py (catalog_release.scaled_nonnegative_integer, the release gate) and phase4-coordinator/internal/billing/rate_global_rounding_cases_test.go (billing.ParseShareBps / billing.ParseMultiplierPPM, what settlement actually computes). Every value is parsed as a binary64 by both readers and scaled by the same binary64 scale, so a case pins the PRODUCT's rounding, not the operator's decimal intent. Two flags mark the vectors that discriminate a WRONG port from math.Round. decimal_divergence: the value's shortest decimal text lands exactly on a half unit while the binary64 product does not, so a Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP port answers one unit higher than the coordinator. floor_half_add_divergence: the product sits immediately BELOW a half unit whose binary64 sum x+0.5 rounds up onto the next integer, so a floor(x+0.5) port answers one unit higher than math.Round, which compares the exact fractional part instead. The boundary vectors were constructed with math.nextafter around each half-unit product, so both the immediately-below and the immediately-above neighbour of a boundary is pinned. Adding a case here binds both sides; changing either implementation alone turns one of them red instead of shipping a signed rate card the coordinator never derives.

shares.note: nextafter below 0.5 bps: the product is 0.49999999999999994, the largest binary64 under a half, and x+0.5 rounds up to exactly 1.0, so a floor(x+0.5) port gives 1
product is exactly the 0.5 bps half unit; ties-to-even would give 0
nextafter below 1.5 bps; decimal ROUND_HALF_UP gives 2
product is exactly the 2.5 bps half unit; ties-to-even would give 2
nextafter below 14.5 bps; decimal ROUND_HALF_UP gives 15
many-digit share above the half unit
production share nudged onto a half unit
rounds up to the full share

multipliers.note: product is exactly the 0.5 ppm half unit; ties-to-even would give 0
product is exactly the 2.5 ppm half unit; ties-to-even would give 2
nextafter below 1000002.5 ppm; decimal ROUND_HALF_UP gives 1000003
product falls just BELOW 1000007.5 ppm; decimal ROUND_HALF_UP gives 1000008
many-digit multiplier above the half unit
